BiblicalUsage: Bethlehem means house of bread, and no town in Scripture carries more weight for its size. Rachel died and was buried on the way to Bethlehem in Genesis 35:19, and Ruth 1:1 opens with a famine driving Elimelech's family out of Bethlehem, then Ruth 1:19 brings Naomi and Ruth back to it. Micah 5:2 looks ahead and names Bethlehem Ephratah as the town from which the ruler of Israel would come.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Bethlehem is God's favourite kind of place: small, hungry, and chosen. The bread of life was born in the house of bread, and I hold that is no accident.
